question.text: Conquistadors from this European nation conquered the Incas. This empire established colonies in all of Central America and most of South America.
question.clue: This country was blamed for a shipwreck near Havana Harbor that destroyed the USS Maine.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about Muslim Spain.
swap.text: This long series of wars between Christians and Muslims for control of Iberia included El Cid. It ended in 1492 when Ferdinand and Isabella accepted Grenada's surrender.
swap.clue: The end of this period was marked by the signing of the Alhambra Decree.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Portuguese colonial history.
question.text: Later modified by the Treaty of Zaragoza to include the Moluccas, this treaty set up a line of demarcation dividing the world between Spain and Portugal.
question.clue: This treaty established a line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, which was later extended through both poles by the Treaty of Zaragoza.

swap.leadin: This fleet attempted to meet with the troops of the Duke of Parma but, while waiting at Gravelines, was attacked by the British navy and was forced to go north.
swap.text: Identify this fleet that King Philip II of Spain sent to conquer England in 1588.
swap.answerHtml: the Spanish Armada [accept Grande y Felicisima Armada or Armada Invencible]
swap.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

question.text: This Catholic king of Spain and successor of Charles V sought the aid of Pope Sixtus V for an invasion of England with the Armada.
question.clue: This ruler commissioned Juan Bautista de Toledo to build a palace complex at El Escorial.

swap.text: This Dominican friar was the first Grand Inquisitor, becoming infamous for his zeal and cruelty.
swap.clue: This confessor of Isabella also led the the Spanish Inquisition as the Grand Inquisitor.

question.leadin: The County of Barcelona and this kingdom were once ruled by a monarchy called its namesake "Crown."
question.text: Name this kingdom whose monarchs included Joanna the Mad and Henry VIII's first wife Catherine.
question.clue: Pope Martin IV ("the fourth") ordered a crusade against this kingdom after its ruler Peter III ("the third") accepted a request to invade Sicily in response to the Sicilian Vespers.

swap.text: Charles V was king of Spain because his father Philip had married Joanna "the Mad," the daughter of these two Catholic Monarchs of Spain. This king and queen kicked the Jews out of Spain in 1492.
swap.answerHtml: Ferdinand II of Aragon [or Ferrando II or Fernando II] AND Isabella I of Castile
swap.clue: He met with the Nasrid ruler Boabdil prior to besieging Granada, which he captured in 1492.

question.text: The Second Macedonian War was prompted by this king's adventures in the Mediterranean, including a defeat at the hands of Rhodes near Chios in 201 BCE. His son Demetrius was restored to him in 190 after keeping the peace with Rome for seven years.
question.clue: This king's opponents claimed that his reign was a violation of the Hague Partition Treaties.

swap.leadin: This monarch's forces defeated Joanna la Beltraneja in a war of succession, allowing her to inherit the throne from Henry IV.
swap.text: Name this queen who presided over the end of the Reconquista when Boabdil surrendered to her.
swap.answerHtml: Isabella I of Castile [or Isabella of Castile; prompt on "Isabella"]
swap.clue: This mother of Juana the Mad conquered the kingdom of Granada and, along with her husband, expelled all Jews from their lands through the Alhambra Decree.

question.leadin: This faction was merged into the FET y de las JONS ("FET ee deh las HONS") in 1937.
question.text: Name this faction that formed as a coalition between right-leaning groups including the Falange and the Carlists. This faction opposed the Republicans in the Spanish Civil War.

swap.leadin: Identify some things about LA RRRRRECONQUISTAAAA!
swap.text: This kingdom founded at the beginning of the Reconquista, and officially recognized under Alfonso II, was centered at Oviedo and captured Galicia and the Pais Vasco in the 9th century.
swap.clue: This kingdom ended when its ruler moved out of its last capital at Oviedo in the Cantabrian Mountains.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the spread of Calvinism out of its birthplace in Switzerland.
question.text: Jeanne d'Albret, a queen of this non-French kingdom, also publicly converted to Calvinism and declared it the state religion in 1560; her son would later claim that "Paris is well worth a mass" when converting to Catholicism.
question.clue: Another ruler of this kingdom was offered the French crown by Etienne Marcel during the Jacquerie.

swap.leadin: Identify the following monarchs with Spanish connections.
swap.text: This king, in power from 1252 to 1284, founded universities at Salamanca and Toledo in addition to promoting Castilian as a scholarly language.
swap.answerHtml: Alfonso X of Castile [or Alfonso the Wise or Alfonso el Sabio; accept translations similar to those above]
swap.clue: It was for this king that Jehuda ben Moses Cohen and Isaac ben Sid assembled namesake astronomical tables.

question.text: This Spanish king who succeeded Franco helped prevent the coup by giving a speech in favor of democracy.
question.clue: This head of state asked Hugo Chavez "Why don't you shut up?" at a meeting where Chavez repeatedly interrupted one of his countrymen.

swap.leadin: This man was exiled after the unauthorized Battle of Cabra, which angered Alfonso VI.
swap.text: Name this man who spent around six years serving the Moorish leader of Zaragoza, during which he frequently fought such Christian kingdoms as Aragon and also earned a nickname that probably means "The Lord."
swap.answerHtml: El Cid (el seed or el theeth) [or Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar; accept El Campeador]
swap.clue: This ruler of Valencia who fought both for and against the Taifa of Zargoza.

question.text: This Basque-born commander of Carlist forces won such battles as Venta de Echavarri and Alsasua before tension with Don Carlos led to his downfall.

swap.leadin: A ruler of this kingdom abdicated the throne to his brother Ramiro and committed himself to a monastery, only to un-retire the following year and join his nephews in defeating the tyrannical Ramiro.
swap.text: Name this medieval Spanish kingdom which broke apart from the larger Kingdom of Asturias in 910 and held dominion over the northwest quarter of the Iberian peninsula.
swap.clue: In a now-discredited theory, the founding of this kingdom was part of a "repopulation" of the "Desert of the Duero."

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Spain's Reconquista communities in the 11th century AD, FTPE.
question.text: The caliphate broke up into these small, independent Islamic states. When the Almoravids emerged from Africa to re-establish control in Muslim Spain, they reabsorbed these states.
question.clue: This states ruled by independent emirs, which were annexed by the Almoravids but re-emerged after the decline of the dynasty. Two of these states were ruled by the Hudids and Aftasids.

swap.leadin: This battle was fought near a hill called La Cabeza near the Guadiana River.
swap.text: Name this 1195 battle, a stunning loss for Alfonso VIII of Castile during the Reconquista. After getting whipped by Abu Yusuf Ya'qub al-Mansur, Alfonso would later avenge this disaster at the Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212.
